question:
Figures \(0,\) \(1,\) \(2,\) and \(3\) consist of \(1,\) \(5,\) \(13,\) and \(25\) nonoverlapping unit squares, respectively. If the pattern were continued, how many nonoverlapping unit squares would there be in figure \(100?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2000_AMC_12_Q08_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The figures grow by adding a layer around the preceding figure. Counting these separate layers avoids having to draw figure \(100\).

Number the layers outward from the central square. For an integer \(k\geq1\), layer \(k\) consists of the squares exactly \(k\) horizontal or vertical unit steps from the center. It has one top square and one bottom square. In each of the \(2k-1\) rows between them, it has two squares, one on each side. Thus layer \(k\) contains
\[
2+2(2k-1)=4k
\]
squares.

Figure \(n\), for a nonnegative integer \(n\), contains the central square and layers \(1\) through \(n\). Every square belongs to exactly one layer, so none is omitted or counted twice. Its total is therefore
\[
1+4(1+2+\cdots+n).
\]
For \(n=100\), pair \(1\) with \(100\), \(2\) with \(99\), and so on. There are \(50\) pairs, each totaling \(101\), so
\[
1+4(1+2+\cdots+100)
=1+4\cdot50\cdot101
=\boxed{20201}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

nodes.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them. For example, express the calculation “add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2” as 2 × (8 + 7). Recognize that 3 × (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.

nodes.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane. For example, given the rule “Add 3” and the starting number 0, and given the rule “Add 6” and the starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting sequences, and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence. Explain informally why this is so.
nodes.label: 5.OA.B.3
